name: Structure: Rule on the chef seat as partner or hire and reconcile the two accounts
text_content:
Extends founder decision 86akh2qrp, which Session 1 filed as a disagreement about who owns culinary identity. Session 2 read both documents in full and found the disagreement runs deeper: the two artifacts may not be describing the same seat.

The white paper says "chef partner": an equal founding partner who "owns the culinary vision" (WP p. 03), freed from carrying the rest of the business (WP p. 05), with an equal vote on whether lunch is built at all (WP p. 36).

The canon says "Executive Chef": a hire, gated by criteria the brand sets. "Mahk standard is an explicit hiring criterion." Held items sit under "pending Executive Chef hire." The relationship to Bangjja Yugi, Baekja, Buncheong and Cheongja is "a hiring criterion." Above it sits the architecture-tier non-negotiable that "culinary identity belongs to the brand, not the chef."

A hiring criterion is an instrument applied to a candidate. It cannot be applied to a founding partner on the same terms.

The ruling decides: the seat's standing in charter and canon versioning; its place in decision rights and in deadlock; whether it sits in the operating agreement or in the point system; and whether Sessions 5 and 6 design the recruitment of a principal or the hiring of an executive.

Requires Dominic. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in section 9 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.
